problems.stem: Informed consent (Belmont Report) requires four conditions. Which set?
problems.explanation: The Belmont Report's four conditions are the canonical framework. AI deployments break each one in characteristic ways.

problems.stem: An interface presents 'Accept All' as a large bright button and 'Reject All' as a three-click trail through nested settings. What dark pattern is this and how does the EU treat it?
options: Asymmetric prominence — defeats voluntariness by making refusal materially costlier than acceptance. Explicitly prohibited by the EU Digital Services Act and targeted by GDPR enforcement and FTC Section 5 actions.
Roach motel; only applies to email.
It is not a dark pattern.
problems.explanation: Asymmetric prominence is one of the best-documented dark patterns. Symmetric controls are required for defensible consent under DSA and GDPR.

problems.stem: Which scenario most clearly shows that consent alone cannot carry the ethical weight, even when perfectly collected?
options: A user clicks 'Accept' on a coffee-shop wifi terms page.
Predictive-policing deployment that affects entire neighborhoods, where individual consent does not address the distributional and democratic question of whether the deployment is appropriate at all.
A user opts into a newsletter.
problems.explanation: Public goods and population-level decisions need democratic deliberation, not aggregated individual clicks. Consent is one layer of many in such cases.

problems.stem: Why is a real, easy withdrawal mechanism (account deletion that actually deletes data, including from training sets where feasible) part of a defensible consent flow?
options: Because consent is meaningful only if it is revocable; without effective withdrawal, the original consent is materially weakened. CCPA and GDPR explicitly establish rights to deletion and erasure.
Because it makes the system faster.
problems.explanation: Revocable consent is the only kind that satisfies voluntariness over time. CCPA right to deletion and GDPR right to erasure operationalize this; current generative architectures still struggle to comply cleanly.
